clinical_category: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control

semantic_correction.stem: During NHSN SSI surveillance, an infection first met superficial-incisional criteria and later, within the same surveillance period, meets deep-incisional SSI criteria. How should the infection-prevention nurse report the event?

options.A: Edit the event type and date to reflect the deeper tissue level where SSI criteria are now met.
options.B: Keep the original superficial classification because the first reported tissue level remains fixed.
options.C: Change the event automatically to organ/space SSI because any progression beyond superficial tissue is organ/space.
options.D: Delete the event because an SSI that changes tissue level during surveillance is no longer reportable.

semantic_correction.rationale: CDC NHSN SSI FAQ Q25 states that when a superficial-incisional SSI progresses and meets criteria at a deeper tissue level within the designated surveillance period, the event type and date of event must be edited to reflect the deepest tissue level where SSI criteria are met. FAQ Q26 separately distinguishes deep-incisional from organ/space infection, so progression to deep tissue does not automatically make the event organ/space. Therefore the existing event should be updated to the deep-incisional level and corresponding event date.
semantic_correction.educational_objective: During NHSN SSI surveillance, update the event type and date when an SSI progresses to a deeper tissue level that meets criteria within the surveillance period.
semantic_correction.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN)
semantic_correction.source_locator: Event Detail — Level of SSI and Application of Site-Specific Definition, Q25: superficial SSI progressing deeper within surveillance period requires editing event type and date to deepest tissue level meeting criteria; Q26: distinguish deep-incisional from organ/space based on tissue involvement
semantic_correction.source_claim_supported: NHSN requires an SSI that progresses to a deeper qualifying tissue level during the surveillance period to be edited so the event type and date reflect the deepest tissue level meeting criteria.
semantic_correction.blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)

semantic_correction.correction_summary_append: RULE1 cleanup: removed the 'never' distractor and unique-length cue, reduced the answer to the exact NHSN reporting action, and used FAQ Q25/Q26 to distinguish deeper incisional progression from organ/space infection.

audit_findings_append.source_locator: SSI FAQ Q25–Q26, last reviewed Jan. 2, 2026
audit_findings_append.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — infection surveillance
audit_findings_append.finding: The original correct answer was uniquely longest and one distractor used an absolute. The revised item directly tests the NHSN event-editing rule with balanced reporting alternatives.

option_audit.A: Correct. NHSN Q25 explicitly requires editing both event type and event date to the deepest qualifying tissue level.
option_audit.B: Incorrect. NHSN does not freeze the original superficial classification when deeper criteria are later met within surveillance.
option_audit.C: Incorrect. Deep-incisional and organ/space SSI criteria are distinct; deeper progression is not automatically organ/space.
option_audit.D: Incorrect. Progression does not make the event nonreportable; NHSN directs the event to be updated.

ambiguity_check: No second defensible answer. A alone follows the current NHSN Q25 instruction for progression within the surveillance period.
cueing_check: All four options are reporting actions of comparable length and specificity; no absolute-word or unique-length cue identifies A.
